title: WrapEntryPointAutoResult
description: Discriminated result: onboarded, or one of three named escalations.

_EntryCandidate.description: One entry-point (or entry-function) candidate in a needs_pick tie.

argv_kind.description: The candidate's classified CLI surface as detect-entry-point read it: argparse / click / typer / hydra / fire / __main__ / console_script / shell — or 'caller_supplied' for a path the detection scan never surfaced (the caller named it), which carries no file-level classification.
argv_kind.title: Argv Kind

function.description: The module-level function name, set only on an entry-FUNCTION tie (several candidate defs inside one resolved file).
function.title: Function

_EntryCandidate.title: _EntryCandidate

_NeedsIntentResult.description: Terminal escalation: a human-owned field is missing.

needs_intent.description: Discriminator: one or more human-owned fields are absent. The deterministic context below is composed and echoed so the caller does not re-scan, but no intent value is invented.
needs_intent.title: Needs Intent

missing_fields.description: The absent fields, dotted as the caller supplies them: 'goal', 'task_generator', 'task_count', 'entry_point.fixed_params.<param>'.
missing_fields.title: Missing Fields

never_invented.description: The subset of missing_fields that code must NEVER fabricate under any 'safe default' rationale (the REQUIRED_CALLER_FIELDS class plus every uncovered entry-point param). Pinned so a future auto-fill has to delete this field to happen.
never_invented.title: Never Invented

ask.description: The precise, named ask — every missing field and why it is caller-owned.
ask.title: Ask

pathway.description: The already-decided pathway, echoed so the caller need not re-derive it.
pathway.title: Pathway

run_name.description: The resolved entry function / wrapper name.
run_name.title: Run Name

argv_kind.description: The resolved entry point's classified CLI surface.
argv_kind.title: Argv Kind

partition.description: The fixed-params partition, present only when it could be computed — i.e. the escalation is an uncovered required param rather than an absent task_generator.

_NeedsIntentResult.title: _NeedsIntentResult

_NeedsPickResult.description: Terminal escalation: an entry-point or entry-function tie.

needs_pick.description: Discriminator: two or more candidates matched with no caller pick. NOTHING was written. The skill refuses to silently pick across main.py / train.py / run.py — a wrong pick is non-recoverable without the user noticing.
needs_pick.title: Needs Pick

reason.description: 'entry_point_tie' = several entry-point FILES matched. 'entry_function_tie' = one file, several candidate module-level defs and no convention (@register_run / `main`) to break it.
reason.title: Reason

candidates.description: Every tied candidate, in detect-entry-point's probe order.
candidates.title: Candidates

resolve_with.description: The exact input field that resolves the tie (e.g. 'entry_point_path').
resolve_with.title: Resolve With

ask.description: The precise, named ask: which value is needed and why code must not pick it.
ask.title: Ask

entry_point_path.description: The already-resolved entry-point file, set on an entry_function_tie.
entry_point_path.title: Entry Point Path

_NeedsPickResult.title: _NeedsPickResult

_NeedsWrapperArgvResult.description: Terminal escalation: the wrapper pathway needs a caller argv + signature.

needs_wrapper_argv.description: Discriminator: direct decoration is structurally blocked and the entry point's CLI surface is not introspectable by this verb, so the argv template + typed signature must come from the caller. NOTHING was written.
needs_wrapper_argv.title: Needs Wrapper Argv

argv_kind.description: Why the surface is not introspectable, named: shell / console_script (no Python signature at all), hydra / click / typer (a decorator rewrote the signature), argparse / __main__ (the flags live in a parser this verb does not read).
argv_kind.title: Argv Kind

pathway_rule.description: The pathway-table row id that routed here (auditable).
pathway_rule.title: Pathway Rule

run_name.description: The name the wrapper will be materialized as.
run_name.title: Run Name

argv_head.description: The leading argv elements code CAN compose from the entry-point shape (['python3', 'train.py'] / ['python3', '-m', 'pkg'] / ['mytool'] / ['./run.sh']). The caller appends the {placeholder} flags.
argv_head.title: Argv Head

argv_extraction.description: detect-entry-point's mechanical-parameter verdict for this entry point, CARRIED THROUGH rather than re-derived. The composite ran the scan in-process to get here, so dropping the verdict would force the caller into a second detect-entry-point call — the produce→consume seam this composite exists to close. 'unsupported' also covers an entry point the caller NAMED that the scan never surfaced (no classified surface to extract from).
argv_extraction.title: Argv Extraction

argv_params.description: The mechanically extracted CLI parameters when argv_extraction == 'extracted', else null. Same shape detect-entry-point emits — see the ArgvParam $def in schemas/detect_entry_point.output.json and the two-honesty-levels rule in hpc_agent/ops/argv_extract.py; not restated here, because a second copy of that shape would drift from the extractor. A param carrying an 'unextracted' marker still needs a source read for the argument it names.
argv_params.title: Argv Params

missing_intent_fields.description: Human-owned fields ALSO still absent — disclosed here so one round trip gathers everything instead of two sequential escalations.
missing_intent_fields.title: Missing Intent Fields

python_module_alternative.description: DISCLOSURE, not a recommendation: SKILL.md:98 offers python_module as the OTHER option for this row, and when the entry point is an importable module the derived {module, function} is named here so the caller can pass entry_point_kind='python_module' instead of an argv template. Code does not choose it, because the discriminator is 'may we edit / must we not edit this file' — caller judgment, not a repo fact. Absent when no dotted path is importable from the campaign dir (a src-layout package, or a non-Python entry point).

ask.description: The precise, named ask: the argv shape needed and why it is not derivable.
ask.title: Ask

_NeedsWrapperArgvResult.title: _NeedsWrapperArgvResult

_OnboardedResult.description: Terminal success: every deterministic step composed.

onboarded.description: Discriminator: the entry point is resolved, the pathway decided, decoration applied (direct-decoration pathway), the frozen YAMLs scanned and the params partitioned. interview_spec is ready.
onboarded.title: Onboarded

pathway.description: 'decorate' = @register_run spliced onto the user's function (SKILL Step 3a, the default). 'wrapper' = the .hpc/wrappers shell_command shim (Step 3b, the rescue boat). 'module' = the python_module dotted-path target, reachable ONLY by explicit caller override (SKILL.md:98's second option for row 2) — it writes nothing at all.
pathway.title: Pathway

pathway_rule.description: The pathway-table row id that decided the pathway (auditable).
pathway_rule.title: Pathway Rule

entry_point_kind.description: The interview entry_point.kind implied by the pathway.
entry_point_kind.title: Entry Point Kind

entry_point_path.description: Resolved entry-point path relative to experiment_dir.
entry_point_path.title: Entry Point Path

entry_point_rule.description: Which rung of the entry-point/function ladder resolved the pick.
entry_point_rule.title: Entry Point Rule

run_name.description: The decorated function / the wrapper's name.
run_name.title: Run Name

argv_kind.description: The resolved entry point's classified CLI surface.
argv_kind.title: Argv Kind

decorated.description: True when this call spliced @register_run onto the function.
decorated.title: Decorated

already_decorated.description: True when the function already carried @register_run (no write).
already_decorated.title: Already Decorated

import_added.description: True when the `from hpc_agent import register_run` import was inserted.
import_added.title: Import Added

frozen_configs.description: Frozen YAMLs (caller override, else the convention scan).
frozen_configs.title: Frozen Configs

frozen_sha_params.description: The <stem>_sha kwarg names the framework threads for each frozen YAML — counted as covered in the partition.
frozen_sha_params.title: Frozen Sha Params

fixed_params.description: Copied VERBATIM from the caller. Empty when the caller supplied none — this verb never synthesizes a constant for an entry-point param.
fixed_params.title: Fixed Params

interview_spec.description: The composed InterviewSpec fragment — goal / task_count / task_generator / entry_point / produced_by — SUBMITTABLE as-is to the `interview` primitive (interview.input.json requires produced_by, so a fragment omitting it could never be handed on unedited). produced_by is the minimal {kind: 'human'} SUGGESTION: the interview's own P1.c composer fills .operator from git config and discloses it as a composed default, so attribution stays required — this verb declares WHO-CLASS, never the identity.
interview_spec.title: Interview Spec

_OnboardedResult.title: _OnboardedResult

_ParamPartition.description: The fixed-params partition over the entry point's declared params.

all_params.description: Every param the entry point declares, in declaration order.
all_params.title: All Params

axis_params.description: Params the task_generator produces per task (plus the <stem>_sha kwargs the framework threads for each frozen YAML). Handled per-task — deliberately absent from fixed_params.
axis_params.title: Axis Params

defaulted_params.description: Params carrying a default in the entry point's own signature. Safe to omit; a caller MAY still pin one for reproducibility.
defaulted_params.title: Defaulted Params

uncovered_params.description: Required (no default), not an axis, and not covered by the caller's fixed_params. Every task would fail on these, so a non-empty list is a needs_intent escalation, never a guess.
uncovered_params.title: Uncovered Params

accepts_var_keyword.description: True when the entry point declares **kwargs, which absorbs any unmatched kwarg — no param can then be 'uncovered'.
accepts_var_keyword.title: Accepts Var Keyword

_ParamPartition.title: _ParamPartition

_PythonModuleTarget.description: A ``python_module`` entry point: an importable dotted module + function.

module.description: Dotted module path importable with the campaign dir on sys.path — derived from the file's location, and only ever offered when every parent directory carries an __init__.py (or the file sits at the repo root). A src-layout package is NOT importable from the repo root, so no dotted path is offered for one.
module.title: Module

function.description: The function inside `module` to treat as the entry point.
function.title: Function

_PythonModuleTarget.title: _PythonModuleTarget
